expectations: Routes the immediate task to exactly one skill, and that skill is cold-email-deliverability.
Treats the absence of sales-context.md as a cold start without asking the user whether this is a cold or a warm start.
Asks at most 7 interview questions, one question per message, with multiple-choice options offered.
Short-list contains between 5 and 8 skills.

No planning skill (sales-motion, sales-icp-definition, sales-market-sizing, sales-account-segmentation, sales-account-tiering, sales-org-structure, sales-quota-setting, sales-pipeline-coverage-modeling, sales-comp-design) appears anywhere in the short-list.
States explicitly that the sender-reputation symptom pinned channel integrity to the top rung of the short-list.
States explicitly that the close date promoted the deal-triage and message/call-asset classes.
Every short-list line names both the bottleneck it attacks and what the session costs.
Anything paying back over a quarter is moved to a Not now list carrying the close date as its unblocking condition, rather than being ranked last on the short-list.
Output contains a Route section, a Short-list section, and a Not now section.
Notes that the authentication/DNS records sit outside the sales team, so the deliverability fix costs an approval and a wait rather than rep hours.
Writes or updates sales-context.md, including one session-log line, before ending the session.
